rationale: The hypothesis that hyperphagia-associated obesity occurs in a discrete subset (<35% frequency) of individuals with LRRC7-related neurodevelopmental disorder (MRD77) is supported by the primary cohort data and subsequent case literature. In the primary discovery study of 33 individuals (Willim et al., 2024), hyperphagia-associated obesity was identified in 'several cases' rather than a majority. Subsequent evaluations (Khan et al., 2026) corroborate that hyperphagia and class-II obesity characterize an age-dependent subset of older individuals rather than being an invariant core finding, preventing false exclusion of LRRC7 variants in non-obese probands.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 33 individuals with heterozygous variants in LRRC7, hyperphagia-associated obesity is reported in 'several cases' alongside core neurodevelopmental features including intellectual disability, autism, ADHD, and aggression.

source.title: Variants in LRRC7 lead to intellectual disability, autism, aggression and abnormal eating behaviors
source.quote: We identify here 33 individuals (one of them previously described) with a dominant neurodevelopmental disorder due to heterozygous missense or loss-of-function variants in LRRC7. The clinical spectrum involves intellectual disability, autism, ADHD, aggression and, in several cases, hyperphagia-associated obesity.

evidence.text: Hyperphagia and class-II obesity were corroborated as being present specifically in a subset of older individuals with LRRC7-related disorder, whereas the infant proband presented with failure to thrive and hypotonia.

source.title: Further Evidence for LRRC7 Gene Involvement in Neurodevelopmental Disorder: A Novel Variant

evidence.text: Diagnostic panels catalog LRRC7 under syndromic monogenic obesity phenotypes due to documented hyperphagia and early-onset obesity.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact longitudinal age of onset and penetrance of hyperphagia and class II/III obesity across a larger international LRRC7 registry?
new_directions.rationale: Early childhood presentation frequently involves hypotonia or failure to thrive before the potential transition to hyperphagic obesity in middle childhood, paralleling Prader-Willi syndrome.
